title: Entropy-sliced KV quantization field lab: FP8/INT8/INT4 fidelity and latency economics
creator: Aisha Kumar
description:
Objective: Run a focused field lab that applies an entropy-sliced quantization strategy to the KV cache to trade GPU memory footprint against generation fidelity and tail latency within our continuous batching runtime. Scope: evaluate FP8, INT8, and INT4 encodings applied selectively by per-key entropy slices and access hotness, measure quality/regression on an internal prompt suite, and quantify end-to-end cost/latency implications for hosted and dedicated modes.

Hypothesis: Partitioning KV entries into low/medium/high-entropy slices and applying progressively lower-bit encodings on low-entropy slices will yield >35% net GPU KV memory reduction with <=3% aggregate quality degradation (measured by embedding cosine drift and generation-token perplexity delta) for most customer workloads. INT4 can provide largest RAM wins but will require staleness-aware fallback to avoid quality cliffs.

Key ideas/novelties:
- Entropy-sliced policy: compute a per-key entropy/variance score during insertion and place entries into 3 slices (hot-high-entropy, mid, cold-low-entropy).
- Quant mapping: hot -> FP8, mid -> INT8, cold -> INT4 (configurable thresholds).
- Access-weighted aging: frequently accessed but low-entropy entries can be promoted to higher-fidelity encoding.
- Inline mixed-kernel execution: update kernel selection logic to handle mixed quant encodings in a single batch without massive memcpy penalties.
- Staleness detector: monitor per-cohort fidelity drift and trigger dynamic rehydrate-to-FP8 when quality drops beyond threshold.

Experiment design:
1) Baselines: FP16 (current prod baseline) and uniform FP8 store across entire KV.
2) Trials: entropy-sliced FP8/INT8/INT4 with three threshold sets (conservative, balanced, aggressive).
3) Workloads: production-sampled traces (privacy-preserving), benchmark prompt-suite (300 prompts across retrieval, summarization, dialogue), and a stress trace with long-context repeat patterns.
4) Metrics:
   - Memory: per-GPU KV bytes allocated and fragmentation delta.
   - Latency: P50/P95/P99 for token generation end-to-end and per-step kernel times.
   - Quality: embedding cosine drift vs FP16, token perplexity delta, and a pass/fail proportion on smoke prompt checks.
   - Stability: incidence of fidelity-triggered rehydrates and fallback rates.
   - Cost proxy: token/s GPU-hour and projected monthly cost delta for hosted tenants.

Implementation plan:
- Phase 0 (lab infra): add profiler/trace flags to capture per-entry entropy and access counters (ETA 2d).
- Phase 1 (impl): encoder/decoder modules for INT4 layout and INT8 with scale-per-slice; integrate quant metadata in KV headers (ETA 1.5w).
- Phase 2 (runtime): kernel selection path that accepts mixed encodings in a batch and performs on-the-fly dequantize into fused cache path; add a lightweight rehydrate job. (ETA 2w).
- Phase 3 (field runs): schedule canary runs on dedicated pool, gather metrics, run A/B vs baseline for 48h slices. (ETA 1w).

Acceptance criteria:
- Balanced config achieves >=35% KV memory reduction vs FP16 with <=3% aggregate quality regressions across the prompt-suite.
- No P99 token latency regression >10% in hosted configuration under normal load.
- Rehydrate/fallback events remain <0.5% of requests in steady-state.

Rollback and safety:
- Canary routes will carry a header to force FP16 paths. Rehydrate policy includes an immediate hard-fallback to FP8 for requests experiencing >5% quality drift. All canaries have kill-switch via runtime flag.

Observability and validation:
- Dashboard cards: per-slice memory usage, dequant latency heatmap, rehydrate rate, embedding-drift histograms.
- Nightly regression job: run prompt-suite against stable anchor for each config and post results to builds dashboard.

Deliverables:
- Code: quant codecs and kernel selector PRs, integration tests.
- Data: field-run metrics, prompt-suite deltas, cost model.
- Playbook: recommended thresholds and rollout steps for runtime-1.24.

Notes: this is intentionally conservative on kernel-level changes; if mixed-kernel complexity introduces unacceptable latency we will fall back to on-device rehydrate paths (dequantify on eviction).
